title: OpenAI
summary: You discovered security flaws in APIs, ChatGPT, Playground, or third-party corporate targets. Note: Content issues like hallucinations are out of scope for bounty but can be reported separately.

title: Google
summary: You found privacy/security attacks, AI-specific vulnerabilities like weight extraction, or prompt injections. Content issues are out of scope for bounty but can be reported via dedicated channels.

title: Anthropic
summary: You discovered critical security vulnerabilities in cybersecurity or high-risk domains (e.g., CBRN). HackerOne program focuses on security issues; jailbreaks are typically out of scope but can be reported to safety channels.

title: Claude
summary: You discovered security flaws in APIs, ChatGPT, Playground, or third-party corporate targets. Note: Content issues like hallucinations are out of scope for bounty but can be reported separately.

title: Hugging Face
summary: You discovered issues with hosted models, datasets (discuss via Discussions tab), or platform/library security vulnerabilities.

title: AI Incident Database
summary: You have knowledge of an AI-related incident that caused harm and has been reported in media or you have direct knowledge of. Submissions are reviewed by editors.

title: AIAAIC Repository
summary: You want to report AI, algorithmic, or automation incidents and controversies, particularly those involving poor ethics, transparency, or accountability.

title: AI Vulnerability Database
summary: You discovered vulnerabilities covering Security, Ethics, and Performance (SEP) issues across the AI lifecycle using CVE-inspired procedures.

title: OECD AI Incidents Monitor
summary: You have information about AI incidents that caused injury, infrastructure disruption, rights violations, or property/environmental harm. Currently does not accept direct submissions but plans to expand.

title: MITRE CVE
summary: You discovered traditional cybersecurity vulnerabilities, including some ML-related security flaws that need CVE assignment.

title: MITRE ATLAS
summary: You want to share real-world AI incidents with the trusted community or contribute to the adversarial tactics knowledge base for AI systems.

title: CISA
summary: You found cybersecurity vulnerabilities in AI systems with potential cybersecurity impact. CISA treats AI as a subset of software systems.

title: CERT
summary: You discovered vulnerabilities that affect multiple vendors, impact safety/critical infrastructure, or when vendor coordination has broken down.

title: NIST
summary: You want to collaborate on research-oriented AI risk assessment, testing, and systematic evaluation of AI systems using frameworks like AI RMF

title: US AI Safety Institute
summary: You want to report issues with AI capabilities assessments, safeguard testing, or collaborate on safety evaluations with national security implications.

title: UK AI Security Institute
summary: You have novel evaluations, agent scaffolding discoveries, or want to participate in their bounty program for AI safety research.
